name: code_read_file

result.evidence:
In src/ingest/parser.ts, parseStatement splits the input text by newline and pops the last line if it is empty:
  const lines = text.split("
");
  if (lines.length > 0 && lines[lines.length - 1] === "") lines.pop();

However, when a CSV file ends with an empty line (or multiple consecutive newlines), splitting by "
" on a string ending with "
" leaves an empty string at the very end of the lines array, which gets popped. If there are multiple trailing newlines (e.g., a file ending with "
" where splitting by "
" leaves an empty string containing "", or consecutive empty trailing lines), or if the bookkeeping software's export adds an empty line followed by a carriage return or another blank line, the popped line is not the empty line causing the failure, or lines still contains an empty string or whitespace-only line at the end that is processed as a data row. Specifically, if the last line has a carriage return ('') or whitespace, lines[lines.length - 1] === "" check fails because the last element is "" or " ", so it is not popped and gets processed as a row, resulting in a 'Malformed row' error.
result.label: bug
